item.title: Percolation on Bidirected Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.28762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study bidirected percolation on an undirected graph $G$: each edge is replaced by two oppositely directed edges, each of which is open independently with probability $p$. Two vertices are strongly connected if they are mutually reachable by open directed paths. Let $p_\mathrm{sc}$ denote the threshold for the existence of an infinite strongly connected cluster, and let $p_c$ denote the usual Bernoulli percolation threshold on $G$. On every transitive amenable graph, we prove that $p_\mathrm{sc}=p_c$. In contrast, sufficiently spread-out modifications of every transitive non-amenable graph satisfy $p_\mathrm{sc}>p_c$. We also show that, on $\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge11$, the expected size of the strongly connected cluster is finite at $p=p_\mathrm{sc}$.
item.dc:creator: Yucheng Liu, Leonardo T. Rolla, Yuliang Shi

item.title: Kinetic Mean-Field Planning via Schr\"odinger Bridges: Existence, Penalization, and Consistency Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.28924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a mean-field planning problem for a swarm of interacting, non-cooperative agents whose dynamics are stochastic and kinetic. The noise acts on the velocity only, and the interaction (of Cucker-Smale type for instance) enters through the drift. For a fixed flow, the problem reduces to a Schr\"odinger bridge problem, and we first prove the existence of an equilibrium by a Schauder fixed-point argument. Then we replace the hard terminal constraint by a penalty function and show that equilibria of the penalized problems converge, along subsequences, to an equilibrium of the original problem. Since equilibria are not unique in general, we instead quantify the consistency error, which measures how far an equilibrium of the penalized problem is from being an equilibrium of the original one. The rate is of order $n^{-1/2}$ for the relative-entropy penalty. The proof relies on the quantitative stability of entropic optimal transport and on a pointwise linear growth bound on the score of the degenerate reference dynamics, which is of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Erhan Bayraktar, Zhiyan Ding, Hiroaki Horikawa

item.title: Functional limit theorems for self-interacting random walks
item.description: arXiv:2610.28935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a wide class of nearest neighbor self-interacting random walks on $\mathbb{Z}$ and show that, under mild conditions, their scaling limits at the process level can be uniquely identified and constructed directly from the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem for their local times, i.e., the joint convergence of rescaled local time ``curves'' of the walks stopped at certain stopping times together with the merge and absorption times of these ``curves'' to a concatenation of coalescing reflected-absorbed diffusions and their merge and absorption times. We apply our results to polynomially self-repelling walks introduced and studied in the mid-90s by B. T\'oth, and to ``true'' self-avoiding walks with bond repulsion. The first application solves a problem that has been open since T\'oth's work: it gives a construction and first properties of a new family of processes, polynomially self-repelling motions, as scaling limits of polynomially self-repelling walks. These processes were simultaneously and independently constructed from flows of correlated powers of Bessel processes by Y. Yu. The second application strengthens an earlier result on convergence of rescaled ``true'' self-avoiding walks to the ``true'' self-repelling motion of B. T\'oth and W. Werner, and streamlines its proof. Our results can be thought of as an ``inversion'' of the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem to get a functional limit theorem for self-interacting random walks.
item.dc:creator: Elena Kosygina, Laure Mar\^ech\'e, Thomas Mountford, Jonathon Peterson

item.title: Free energy and fluctuations of generalized bipartite Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models and generalized Hopfield models
item.description: arXiv:2610.29055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the free energy of generalized bipartite Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models in the high temperature regime, with one spin normalized and the other either normalized or i.i.d. We derive a unified formula for the limiting free energy in both settings. We also prove that the fluctuations of the free energy converge to a Gaussian distribution under mild assumptions. The proof is based on a bipartite multigraph expansion, which also gives free energy results for generalized Hopfield models and log likelihood ratio of spiked rectangular models.
item.dc:creator: Hyunsuk Choo, Ji Oon Lee

item.title: Refined Cram\'er-type moderate deviations by Stein's method under dependence
item.description: arXiv:2610.29078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish refined Cram\'er-type moderate deviations for dependent random variables at any fixed order $m\geq3$. Combining higher-order Stein identities with exponential tilting, we obtain cumulant-corrected tail approximations with explicit error bounds for boundedly supported kernels. Our main application gives a fourth-order expansion under bounded local dependence, reaching an $O(n^{3/10})$ deviation range under standard normalization with fixed dependence parameters. It improves on previous work in both deviation range and applicability, and also covers bounded $m$-dependent sequences without an independent-base representation. Further applications to the generalized combinatorial central limit theorem and the Curie-Weiss model also extend some earlier results under permutation and mean-field dependence.
item.dc:creator: Hui-Lin Liu, Song-Hao Liu, Dawei Lu

item.title: Conditional Reflected Backward Stochastic Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.29103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new type of reflected backward stochastic differential equations (reflected BSDEs), referred to as conditional reflected BSDEs, in which the conditional expectation of the Y-component of the solution with respect to a given sub-{\sigma}-algebra appears in both the generator and the obstacle. Under a Lipschitz condition on the loss function with sufficiently small Lipschitz constants, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution for both the case of Lipschitz generator and the case of quadratic generator, bounded terminal value and bounded loss function. When the generator has quadratic growth and the terminal value and loss function are unbounded, we establish the uniqueness with the help of {\theta}-method. Finally, a penalization approximation scheme holds under an additional monotonicity structure imposed on the generator and the loss function, without any restriction on the Lipschitz constants of the loss function.
item.dc:creator: Hanwu Li

item.title: Normal approximation, moderate and large deviations for the elephant random walk with stops and random step sizes
item.description: arXiv:2610.29105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the elephant random walk with stops and independent positive random step sizes. Building on fixed-movement estimates, we obtain quantitative normal approximations for an empirically normalized statistic by controlling its random denominator and the independent movement clock. A permutation comparison preserves the diffusive Kolmogorov rate, while variance matching permits third-order Zolotarev estimates. We also derive self-normalized Cram\'er-type moderate deviations. For regularly varying step-size tails, we obtain uniform precise large deviations and establish the necessity of the diffusive and critical threshold orders. Further applications of the clock representation yield large deviation principles for Weibull-type and light-tailed step sizes, and a precise light-tailed expansion in the balanced case.
item.dc:creator: Shuyuan Liang

item.title: Normal approximation and self-normalized moderate deviations for the minimal random walk with random step sizes
item.description: arXiv:2610.29156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the minimal random walk with independent positive random step sizes. By separating the movement count from the centered step-size noise, we obtain normal approximations and self-normalized Cram\'er-type moderate deviations under finite-moment assumptions. For the noise, conditioning on the movement count yields Kolmogorov, Wasserstein and Zolotarev bounds. A polynomial moderate-deviation range holds when a recalled stop can lead to movement. At the boundary where this probability is zero, we obtain a logarithmic range and construct a bounded nonsymmetric example excluding a general polynomial range. For the full position, a weighted martingale representation gives limit laws in the different regimes, nonuniform normal approximations and moment-distance bounds without logarithmic losses. Variance concentration also yields self-normalized moderate deviations in the diffusive and critical regimes.
item.dc:creator: Shuyuan Liang

item.title: Small deviations for integrators in terms of It\^{o}--Wiener expansions
item.description: arXiv:2610.29202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate small deviations for a class of Gaussian processes, known as integrators. In general, such processes are non-Markovian and may even fail to be semimartingales. First, we investigate small deviations for the multi-dimensional Wiener process, focusing on the asymptotic behavior of the Fourier--Wiener transform of the associated hitting event. We analyze the Fourier--Wiener transform and the separate summands in its It\^{o}--Wiener expansion. Then, we establish the asymptotic limits of the associated multiple integrals with heat kernels. Finally, we obtain the small deviation asymptotic result for the integrator $\eta$ associated with the continuous linear operator.
item.dc:creator: Qingsong Wang, A. A. Dorogovtsev

item.title: A New Modification of the Milstein Method and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
item.description: arXiv:2610.29206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The article presents a new modification of the Milstein method for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the first author in 2006. The article also provides the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Dmitriy F. Kuznetsov, Mikhail D. Kuznetsov

item.title: Temporal-Logical Stochastic Processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.29209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a measure-theoretic framework for Temporal-Logical Stochastic Processes (TLSP), in which temporal-logic specifications induce time-indexed stochastic observables capturing the robustness of temporal satisfaction. Building upon existing probabilistic interpretations of temporal-logic robustness, we systematically investigate the stochastic-process structure of these observables. We establish their measurability, shifted-filtration adaptedness, and sample-path regularity under suitable assumptions, and characterize the action of temporal operators on stochastic processes. We derive pathwise perturbation bounds and quantify the sensitivity of temporal satisfaction probabilities through the probability mass concentrated near the logical boundary. A topology on the observable-process space and a semantic pseudometric on temporal formulas are introduced to establish convergence of temporal-logical observables under perturbations of formula parameters and temporal intervals. We further characterize conditions ensuring weak convergence of observable-process distributions and convergence of temporal satisfaction probabilities. Finally, we establish a process-level large-deviation principle for temporal-logical observables, providing a variational characterization of rare temporal events through minimum-action trajectories. The resulting framework connects temporal-logic semantics with stochastic-process topology, stability, convergence, and rare-event asymptotics, providing a mathematical foundation for the analysis of temporally constrained stochastic systems.
item.dc:creator: Venkatraman Renganathan

item.title: Higher-order convex orders under free multiplicative convolution
item.description: arXiv:2610.29258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that free multiplicative convolution with a probability measure on $[0,\infty)$ preserves the $k$-convex order for every integer $k\ge2$, assuming finite $(k-1)$st absolute moments for the two measures being compared and for the convolving measure. The compared measures may have arbitrary support in $\mathbb{R}$.
item.dc:creator: Cheng-Xuan Soong

item.title: Tamed Euler Approximation of Invariant Measures for Weakly Interacting Particle Systems and McKean--Vlasov Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.29314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze explicit tamed Euler approximations for weakly interacting particle systems and McKean--Vlasov diffusions with additive noise and polynomially weighted locally H\"older, possibly superlinear drift.Under dissipativity at infinity and suitable stability assumptions, we establish time-uniform $W_1$ bounds by reflection coupling, separating relaxation, time-discretization, and finite-particle errors.For small step sizes, we prove existence and uniqueness of numerical invariant laws and bound their error relative to the continuous-time particle invariant law uniformly in $N$ in a normalized joint $W_1$ distance. We further bound the error of the one-particle numerical invariant marginal relative to the McKean--Vlasov invariant law by $O(\theta^{\min\{\alpha,\beta/2\}}+N^{-1/2})$, where $\theta$ is the step size, $N$ the particle number, $\alpha\in(0,1/2]$ the taming exponent, and $\beta\in(0,1]$ the H\"older exponent. Analytical examples illustrate the framework for smooth and non-Lipschitz drifts.
item.dc:creator: Lingyan Cheng, Ruinan Li, Shiyu Liu, Wei Liu

item.title: Subsequential Version of Breiman's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.29551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study randomly weighted sums \[ T_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n X_iY_i}{\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i}, \] where $(X_i)$ and $(Y_i)$ are independent sequences of i.i.d. random variables, with nonnegative weights $Y_i$, motivated by Breiman's conjecture. We introduce the class $ISSV$ of $I$-subsequentially slowly varying tails and establish a subsequential analogue of Darling's maximum--sum theorem. This provides a subsequential generalization of Breiman's slowly varying theorem and, as a corollary, resolves the slowly varying case of his conjecture. We also establish a subsequential analogue of Breiman's nonzero-index theorem, characterizing the existence of nondegenerate subsequential limits, distinct in distribution from $X_1,$ by the failure of slow variation of the integrated tail, for weight $Y_1$ with tail distributions outside the class $ISSV$. Finally, we formulate the subsequential separation principle, prove it under a finite-second-moment assumption, and show that its general validity would imply the nonzero-index case of Breiman's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Volodymyr Pavlenkov

item.title: Inhomogeneous random graphs: how heavy tails reshape connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.29564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study inhomogeneous random graphs on $n$ vertices with independent Pareto weights of parameter $\alpha>0$ and connection probabilities $\min(\varepsilon_n W_iW_j, 1)$. Our main focus is the infinite-mean regime $0<\alpha<1$. Under the scaling $n\varepsilon_n^\alpha=\lambda$, with $\lambda>0$ fixed, the global architecture of the graph is entirely governed by the Poisson point process $\Pi$ of rescaled extreme weights. In particular, the size of the largest component, divided by $n$, converges to a non-degenerate random variable expressed as an explicit functional of $\Pi$. Through the point process $\Pi$, we also characterize the exact limiting connectivity probability, uncovering a non-sharp connectivity threshold. The second largest component and the diameter of the largest component are bounded with high probability. The distance between two uniformly chosen vertices in the largest component is at most three with high probability. We also prove convergence of the point process of rescaled degrees and identify the limiting distribution of the maximum degree. For completeness, we obtain expected degree asymptotics, typical degree limits and connectivity regimes for all $\alpha>0$. Due to the failure of classical branching process approximations in the infinite-mean regime, our approach relies fundamentally on analyzing the extreme weight environment $\Pi$.
item.dc:creator: Luisa Andreis, Luca Avena, Rajat Subhra Hazra, Elena Matteini

item.title: Wave equation with unbounded terms driven by a stochastic measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.29648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The one-dimensional wave equation with additive noise driven by a stochastic measure is considered. For the stochastic integrator, we assume only the sigma-additivity in probability and that $|y|^\tau$ is integrable on $\mathbb{R}$ for some $\tau>1/2$. The class of stochastic measures includes many important cases of random processes. In the equation, the stochastic measure depends only on the spatial variable. The existence, uniqueness, and H\"{o}lder regularity of the mild solution are proved. In the previous publications, similar results were obtained for the case of bounded terms of the wave equation driven by a stochastic measure. In our paper, one term may be unbounded, satisfying the linear growth condition. Nevertheless, we prove that the solution is bounded in this case.
item.dc:creator: Mykhailo Debeliak, Vadym Radchenko

item.title: Weighted Risk Aggregation under Long-Memory Dependence: Pathwise Fluctuations of Exposure-Weighted Losses
item.description: arXiv:2610.29743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We model insurance loss in each period as deterministic exposure multiplied by a nonnegative function of a long-memory Gaussian sequence. A weighted law of the iterated logarithm yields the exact almost-sure scale and sharp constant of centered cumulative loss. Loss per unit of cumulative exposure converges almost surely to its mean, with an exact error scale common to all admissible exposure profiles; the sharp constant depends on the exposure exponent. Lognormal and quadratic examples, of Hermite ranks one and two, and a simulation illustrate the results. A known spectral formula expresses the quadratic coefficient through a leading eigenvalue.
item.dc:creator: Elina Moldavskaya

item.title: A branching model for selective sweeps
item.description: arXiv:2610.29759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At every discrete time i we introduce exactly one individual whose genotype is given by a p_i sampled uniformly in (0,1). This individual will be the founder of a branching process with a geometric offspring distribution with parameter p_i. All the branching processes are independent. We show that as time goes to infinity successive selective sweeps occur. That is, ever more fit single genotypes dominate the population. Moreover, at any fixed time we prove that the dominating genotype is not the most fit genotype. Finally, we show that the rescaled point process associated to selective sweeps converges to an inhomogeneous Poisson process.
item.dc:creator: Luiz Renato Fontes, Rinaldo B. Schinazi

item.title: A paintbox characterization of labeled partitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.29824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study pairs of labeled random partitions $(\Pi,\tau)$ with a finite label set $E$, which can be thought of as a random mutation and coalescence mechanism of a countable number of blocks. Labeled exchangeable partition probability functions (LEPPFs) are defined via labeled analogues of Kingman's paintbox partitions. They satisfy normalization, symmetry and consistency in a multivariate sense. Under an \emph{equivariance condition}, a representation for $(\Pi,\tau)$ in terms of labeled paintbox partitions is derived, leading to a full characterization of LEPPFs by a unique probability measure $G$. This representation is extended to \emph{jointly exchangeable and consistent} transition pairs using a product measure $F \otimes G$. These results yield a one-to-one correspondence between distributions of jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs and pairs of exchangeable distributions and LEPPFs.
item.dc:creator: Maximilian Flamm, Martin M\"ohle

item.title: Spatial preferential attachment models: robustness revisited
item.description: arXiv:2610.29853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate robustness under percolation in the degree-driven spatial preferential attachment model. Consider a profile that is regularly varying with exponent $-\delta$, where $\delta>1$, and an attachment rule with asymptotic slope $\gamma\in(0,1)$. Jacob and M\"orters (Ann. Probab. 45 (2017)) proved robustness when $$ \delta\left(\frac1\gamma-1\right)<1. $$ We prove the converse in the strict regime: if $$ \delta\left(\frac1\gamma-1\right)>1, $$ then sufficiently strong Bernoulli vertex thinning destroys the giant component. In particular, the strict robustness boundary coincides with that of the age-dependent random connection model.
item.dc:creator: Peter Gracar, Christian M\"onch

item.title: Competitive Lotka-Volterra systems with random catastrophes: invasion fitnesses and reversal of the competitive hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2610.29888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a two-type individual-based population with logistic competition subject to random catastrophes: at the epochs of a Poisson process, each individual survives independently with a random, type-dependent probability. In the large-population limit, the process converges to a competitive Lotka-Volterra system perturbed by multiplicative jumps. We show that the long-time behaviour of this system -exclusion of one type or the other, or coexistence -is governed by two averaged invasion fitnesses, obtained from the classical ones by replacing each growth rate a i with its average {\=a}i = a i + rE[ln $\Theta$ (i) ], where r is the catastrophe rate and $\Theta$ (i) is the survival probability of an individual of type i when a catastrophe occurs. A consequence is that catastrophes can reverse the competitive hierarchy: a type doomed to exclusion in the deterministic system may persist or even exclude its competitor, when catastrophes are frequent enough, even if each catastrophe is individually more harmful to it. In the finite population setting, we also study the invasion of a mutant on the time scale ln K, where K is a scaling parameter, through a coupling with branching processes in the varying random environment generated by the resident population.
item.dc:creator: Eug\`ene Ferragu (MICROCOSME, LIPhy), Aline Marguet (MICROCOSME, LIPhy), Charline Smadi (UR LESSEM, UGA)

item.title: Kelly's conjectures on Condorcet winner probabilities for odd electorates
item.description: arXiv:2610.29904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $C(m,n)$ denote the probability that, among $n$ independent uniformly random permutations of $m$ labels, there exists a label that precedes every other label in a strict majority of the permutations. We prove that $C(m,n)>C(m,n+2)$ for $m \ge 3$ and odd $n \ge 1$, and that $C(m,n)>C(m+1,n)$ for $m \ge 2$ and odd $n \ge 3$. These results establish Kelly's two monotonicity conjectures for odd electorates. The proofs use integral representations involving probabilities associated with sums of independent Bernoulli random variables.
item.dc:creator: Seick Kim, Hocheol Shin

item.title: Painlev\'e representations for joint moments of characteristic polynomials from the orthogonal and unitary symplectic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.29947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study joint moments of characteristic polynomials and their second derivatives for Haar-distributed matrices from the unitary symplectic and orthogonal groups. We establish their large-$N$ asymptotics throughout the full admissible range of the moment parameters and identify the limiting coefficients probabilistically in terms of the first inverse power sum of the Bessel point process. This extends the corresponding results of Assiotis, Gunes, Keating, and Wei [Proc. Lond. Math. Soc., 132 (2026), e70136] to the full admissible parameter range. Throughout this full range, we also express these limits in terms of a distinguished solution of the $\sigma$-Painlev\'e III' equation. Our approach reduces the problem to singular inverse-power statistics of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and combines their finite-$N$ $\sigma$-Painlev\'e V representation with a refined Riemann-Hilbert analysis yielding precise small-$x$ asymptotics and uniform derivative estimates for the finite-$N$ correction term. A key ingredient in the probabilistic identification is a kernel-based proof that the rescaled first inverse power sum of the Jacobi ensemble converges in distribution to its Bessel point process counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Theodoros Assiotis, Thomas Bothner, Jonathan P. Keating, Nicholas Simm, Fei Wei

item.title: Differentiability of Shape Function for Piecewise Smooth Lagrangians in Poissonian Random Environments
item.description: arXiv:2610.29966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a family of models of directed first passage percolation type in continuous multi-dimensional Euclidean space and discrete time with admissible paths constrained to visiting a Poissonian point at each step. We show that even if the Lagrangian defining the cost or energy of a step is allowed to have gradient discontinuities, the resulting shape function, or effective Lagrangian, belongs to the class C1 and provide a formula for its gradient. We also study the limit shapes for the associated growth model. We show that the part of the boundary of the limit shape that can be called the effective front is also C1, and we describe the complementary part, the footprint. We include a study of several concrete examples and several simulations.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Bakhtin, Benjamin Edidin

item.title: On Divisibility Properties of Zipf Law and Relatives
item.description: arXiv:2610.29974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe recursive chance mechanisms and processes involving Zipf's law and relatives, all showing up mixing properties, both geometric and Poisson. Relations to Markov processes are explored.
item.dc:creator: Thierry E Huillet (LPTM - UMR 8089)

item.title: Tempered Langevin diffusions with polynomial-tailed targets: explosions, moment thresholds and ergodicity
item.description: arXiv:2610.30024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For tempered Langevin diffusions (TLDs) targeting polynomially tailed measures, the convergence rate is known to change from polynomial to exponential to uniform as the temperature rises through a critical value. We explain this transition by the tails of the marginal laws of the norm of the TLD, up to a second, larger critical temperature beyond which the TLD explodes. As the temperature increases, these tails change from stretched-exponential, through super-polynomial at the first critical temperature, to polynomial, mirroring the transition in the convergence rate. Moreover, this tail analysis gives a complete quantification of the convergence rates throughout the non-explosive regime, in both $f$-variation and Wasserstein distances.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandar Mijatovi\'c, Haokai Xie

item.title: On the proof of the Kozma-Nitzan conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.30063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this short note, we give an exposition of the recent proof of the Kozma-Nitzan conjecture provided by OpenAI.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Baptiste Gou\'er\'e (IDP)

item.title: Mellin transformed exponential volumes and probabilistic moduli spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.26580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A decorated surface is a surface with boundary and a finite set of marked boundary points called cusps. We continue to study the exponential volumes E(S,K,L) of moduli spaces of ideal hyperbolic structures on a decorated surface S, with the given values of lengths of boundary geodesic circles L and boundary geodesic intervals K, introduced in our previous work: 1. We prove that the Mellin--Laplace transform of E(S,K,L) admits Barnes integral presentations, and satisfies recursions, generalising Mirzakhani's recursions. 2. We specify a subset I of the blue boundary intervals, and assign to them any collection of weights. We show that the Mellin transform of the function E(S,K,L) along the variables K at the blue intervals, evaluated at the weights values, calculates weighted exponential volumes of various moduli spaces. If all boundary intervals are blue and all weights are 1/2, we recover Chekhov's volumes of moduli spaces of hyperbolic surfaces with crowns, discretizing the Schwarzian action. We derive recursions for the weighted exponential volumes. 3. We introduce probabilistic Teichmuller spaces related to decorated surfaces S. They are infinite dimensional and carry canonical Wiener type measures. The definition of the measures builds on the works of Bauerschmidt - Losev - Wildemann and Losev. Their quotients by the action of the modular group of S are probabilistic moduli spaces. We show that their volumes are finite. We prove recursion formulas for these measures, and hence for the volumes. The emerging theory generalizes the Schwarzian field theory of Stanford - Witten from the disc to any decorated surfaces, i.e. to open string format. In particular, we get recursions for the Feynman integrals in Schwarzian field theory on decorated surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Alexander B. Goncharov, Zhe Sun

item.title: Wavelet covariances under fixed finite observations: dilation symmetry breaking and distinct endpoint limits
item.description: arXiv:2610.28665v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a centered homogeneous generalized Gaussian field with spectral weight $C|\omega|^{-\gamma}$, we prove two-endpoint recovery of normalized posterior wavelet covariances under fixed finite admissible observations. Global dilation symmetry holds if and only if all observation functions vanish. The nonzero wavelet and the observation functions are real Schwartz functions with $M\geq1$ vanishing moments, with $C>0$ and $\gamma<2M+1$. Noise is Gaussian and field-independent, and total observation covariance is positive definite. Under simultaneous dilation of target scales and positions, multiplication by $\lambda^{-\gamma}$ recovers the prior covariance as $\lambda\downarrow0$ and $\lambda\uparrow\infty$, uniformly on every fixed compact target set. If a nonzero observation function exists, additional finite first nonzero Fourier orders $m_\psi,m_i$ at zero of the wavelet and nonzero observation functions yield compact-uniform recovery bounds $O(\lambda^{2m_\psi+1-\gamma})$ and $O(\lambda^{-(2\min_i m_i+1-\gamma)})$, with leading coefficients and cancellation-dependent improvements. The bounds are exact leading orders when their coefficients are nonzero. For the Mat\'ern-type spectrum $S(\omega)=C(\kappa^2+\omega^2)^{-p}$, $\kappa>0$, $1/2<p<M+1/2$, fixed finite noisy point observations yield distinct compact-uniform limits: the homogeneous $C|\omega|^{-2p}$ kernel after multiplication by $\lambda^{-2p}$ at small scales, and the constant-spectrum $S(0)$ kernel without normalization at large scales. A projection-norm criterion treats fixed closed observation subspaces; Mexican-hat formulas illustrate the finite-observation results.
item.dc:creator: Jun Tsuzurugi

item.title: Universality of approximate message passing under a fourth-moment tail condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.28971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove state evolution for approximate message passing (AMP) with rectangular random matrices whose entries are independent, centered, and variance-normalized. The row and column dimensions grow with a ratio that converges to a positive finite limit. The entry laws may differ across coordinates and dimensions, and we assume uniform integrability of the fourth powers of the rescaled entries. For entries sampled independently from a fixed law, a finite fourth moment suffices, with no requirement for higher moments. The nonlinearities are continuously differentiable and globally Lipschitz, with bounded continuous first state derivatives. The signal and noise have independent and identically distributed coordinates with finite moments of all orders, and are independent of each other and of the matrix. At every fixed number of iterations, empirical averages of pseudo-Lipschitz functions of order two converge in probability to the limits specified by Gaussian state evolution. These averages include empirical second moments and products of trajectory coordinates. The proof combines an aggregate bound on third derivatives with randomized Lindeberg replacement and operator-norm truncation, without matching third moments or invoking a non-Gaussian universality theorem. We also show that independence of complementary projected components for every deterministic rank-one constraint pair characterizes Gaussian entries. This identifies the limitation of extending Gaussian conditioning identities to independent non-Gaussian matrices. Finally, a variance-profile example shows that average variance normalization alone does not ensure the homogeneous state evolution limits.
item.dc:creator: Ripunjay Dwivedi, Taejoon Kim

item.title: A Jump-Modified Wasserstein Gradient Flow for Maximum Mean Discrepancy with Energy Kernels
item.description: arXiv:2610.29007v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a jump-modified Wasserstein gradient flow of the squared maximum mean discrepancy generated by the energy kernels $K(z)=-|z|^q$, $0<q<2$, in every dimension $d\ge2$ as well as the one-dimensional range $1\le q<2$. Under subcritical density and finite-moment assumptions, we prove global well-posedness. The added jumps transfer mass toward smaller values of the first variation and dissipate the same MMD energy as the transport term. Under our hypotheses on the target and jump rates, every Borel probability measure with finite MMD energy and zero jump dissipation is equal to the target. Combining this rigidity with compactness and a second-moment identity yields convergence to the target from finite-second-moment data, without additional uniform-in-time density or moment assumptions. We also construct a global collision-free particle process whose energy is nonincreasing along each path. A quantitative mean-field estimate applies to general initial empirical approximations, including deterministic configurations; propagation of chaos for exchangeable data and long-time target approximation follow as consequences.
item.dc:creator: Ansh Desai, Jason Liu, Srujan Roplekar, Matthew Rosenzweig

item.title: Third and Fourth Moment Phenomena for Monochromatic Edges and Applications to Graph-Based Two-Sample Tests
item.description: arXiv:2610.29215v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a graph sequence $\{G_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, denote by $T_n$ the number of monochromatic edges when the vertices of $G_n$ are independently colored red or blue with probabilities $p$ and $1-p$, respectively. We characterize the asymptotic normality of $T_n$, after centering and scaling to unit variance, in terms of subgraph (motif) counts and standardized moments. One of the highlights of our results is a {\it third moment phenomenon}: for every fixed $p\in(0,1)\backslash\{\frac12\}$, asymptotic normality holds if and only if the standardized third moment converges to zero. The more familiar {\it fourth moment condition}, which requires the standardized fourth moment to converge to $3$, gives an equivalent characterization except at the two exceptional probabilities $p=\frac{1\pm1/\sqrt3}{2}$. At these values, the standardized fourth moment converges to $3$ for every graph sequence with a diverging number of edges, even when Gaussian convergence fails. In contrast, in the balanced case $p=\frac12$, the fourth moment condition characterizes asymptotic normality, while the third moment condition is insufficient. These results identify three distinct regimes for moment characterizations of Gaussian convergence, determined by the coloring probability. We further show that the third moment condition remains sufficient in the sparse regime, where $p=p_n \to 0$. As an application, we derive the limiting null distribution of two-sample statistics based on undirected $K$-nearest-neighbor graphs in the Poissonized setting, identifying sharp growth conditions on $K$ for asymptotic normality.
item.dc:creator: Siva Athreya, Bhaswar B. Bhattacharya, Yogesh Dahiya, Karambir Das, Spandan Ghoshal, Sourish Maniyar, Elizabeth Sara Roy

item.title: Strongly log-concave measures and lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.29238v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full rank lattice with the property that $\det \Gamma \ge 1$ for all sublattices $\Gamma \subseteq \Lambda^*$. We prove that there exists a symmetric random vector $X \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with a smooth, strictly positive density $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying that $f$ is $\alpha$-strongly log-concave, where $\alpha = 2\pi/e$, and $X + \Lambda$ is uniform on $\mathbb{R}^n/\Lambda$. Moreover, we show that the existence of such a density $f$ characterizes the assumption on $\Gamma$ up to a constant. There are a few consequences of the above. First, for such lattices we can bound the covering radius \[ \mu(\Lambda, K) = \max_{x \in \mathbb{R}^n} \min_{\lambda \in \Lambda} \|x-\lambda\|_K \le \sqrt{\frac{2e}{\pi}} \cdot \mathbb{E}_G\, \|G\|_K \] of a convex body $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $0$ in its interior, where $G \sim N(0,I)$. This implies an $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ bound for the flatness constant and an $O(\log^{3/2} n)$ bound for the subspace flatness constant. Second, we establish as a consequence an alternative proof of the reverse Minkowski theorem with an explicit constant.
item.dc:creator: Brayden Letwin, Victor Reis, Thomas Rothvoss

item.title: Sharp asymptotics for a free boundary touching a degenerate boundary: the perpetual Heston put
item.description: arXiv:2610.29253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the exercise boundary of the perpetual American put in the Heston model near zero variance. There the pricing operator degenerates, and the exercise boundary, a free boundary in the stock--variance half-plane, touches the boundary of the half-plane. No Feller condition is imposed. The boundary is analytic at positive variance and extends as a regular $C^1$ curve tangent to the zero-variance axis. Its approach to the axis follows one of three laws, according to whether the Feller ratio $2\kappa\theta/\sigma^2$ is larger than, equal to, or smaller than one: a logarithmic correction to linear order, an exponential correction in the square root of the logarithm, or a fractional power. In the first two cases the leading coefficients are explicit and the tangent is not H\"older continuous at the axis. In the third case the exponent is selected by a possibly nonsymmetric stable operator on the axis, and the amplitude is finite and positive.
item.dc:creator: Takwon Kim, Junkee Jeon, Jehan Oh

item.title: Statistics of entries of matrices from the general linear group over a finite field
item.description: arXiv:2610.29305v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ be the group of $n\times n$ invertible matrices over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. How many matrices in $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ are there with a subset of their entries prescribed? Motivated by the random matrix theory of classical compact groups, we address this question and various variants, with a focus on asymptotic results that are valid as $n$ tends to infinity. Our methods are Fourier-analytic, with the main input being an exponential sum over $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, evaluated in 1955 by Hodges via elementary methods. Our results turn out to be related to investigations carried out in other fields, including coding theory, universality for $p$-adic matrices and algebraic combinatorics.
item.dc:creator: Ofir Gorodetsky

item.title: The first $\ell^2$-Betti number, cost and rank gradient of few-relator random groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.29502v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a random group in the few-relator model with $n\ge 2$ generators and $m\ge 1$ relators. We prove that asymptotically almost surely the first $\ell^2$-Betti number, the cost minus one, and the absolute rank gradient of $G$ are all equal to $\max\{n-m-1,0\}$. In particular, the equality $\beta_1^{(2)}(G)=0$ when $m\ge n-1$ answers positively a conjecture of Kielak, Kropholler and Wilkes [J. Lond. Math. Soc., 2022].
item.dc:creator: Miguel Donoso-Echenique, Eduardo Silva

item.title: Continuity of Furstenberg entropy on Bowen Poisson bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.29561v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide a sufficient criterion for continuity of the Furstenberg entropy of Bowen Poisson bundles, jointly in the random walk measure and the underlying invariant random subgroup. The criterion applies in particular for tree-like Poisson bundles of a free group and for intersectional invariant random subgroups on lamplighter groups. It also provides continuity of the boundary entropy spectrum of powers of prime measured groups.
item.dc:creator: J\'er\'emie Brieussel, Hanna Oppelmayer

item.title: On the notion of reasonable functions in Cohen--Lenstra type heuristics
item.description: arXiv:2610.29880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We elucidate the notion of "reasonable functions" in the context of Cohen--Lenstra heuristics. For a sequence $(x_i)_i$ of independent random variables valued in an infinite discrete probability space $(X,p)$, we investigate for what sets $S$ of functions on $X$ it is true that almost surely, for all $f\in S$, the average of $f$ on the sequence is equal to its expected value. We show that if $p$ decays sufficiently quickly, as e.g. the Cohen--Lenstra distribution does, then $\bigcup_{q>1}L^q(X)$ is such a set; while if $p$ decays sufficiently slowly, then not even $\bigcap_{q<\infty}L^q(X)$ has this property.
item.dc:creator: Alex Bartel, Adam Morgan

item.title: Squarefree values of random polynomials are Gaussian mixtures
item.description: arXiv:2610.29911v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fix $d\ge1$ and choose a polynomial $P$ uniformly at random from the set of integer polynomials of degree $d$ whose coefficients have absolute value at most $H$. We study $E_{P}$, the error in the count of squarefree values $P(n)$ for $n\leq x$. In the range $x=H^{o\left(1\right)}$, we prove that $E_{P}\left(x\right)/x^{\frac{1}{4}}$ converges to a Gaussian mixture that is not itself Gaussian, $\sqrt{C\left(G\right)}Z$, where $G$ is the weak limit, as $H\rightarrow\infty$, of the prime-indexed vector $\left(P\bmod p^{2}\right)_{p}$, $C$ is a nonnegative function and $Z$ is an independent standard Gaussian. This answers a question of Sofos. Finally, in the appendix, we establish that $\log \mathbb{E}[C(G)^m]\asymp_d m^2/(\log m)^2$ as $m\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Omer Simhi

item.title: Normal form approach to unconditional well-posedness of the periodic stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equation with an additive noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.29935v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a stochastic normal form method for stochastic dispersive equations. As a model example, we study the stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equation (SKdV) with an additive noise, posed on the circle. By replacing integration by parts (in time) in the deterministic setting with Ito's product formula in the current stochastic setting, we transform SKdV with an additive noise into a stochastic normal form equation with additive and multiplicative noises. We then use the stochastic normal form equation to prove optimal pathwise unconditional global well-posedness of SKdV in $L^2(\mathbb{T})$.
item.dc:creator: Damiano Greco, Tadahiro Oh, Philippe Sosoe, Yuzhao Wang

item.title: Self-normalized Bernstein Inequalities for Regenerative Processes and Applications to Learning Without Independence
item.description: arXiv:2610.30119v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a self-normalized Bernstein inequality for bounded functions of a regenerative process with independent, identically distributed marked cycles of finite mean length. The bound uses observed cycle lengths and retains explicit terms for truncation and the cycle ending after the observation horizon. Selecting a tuning parameter from a finite deterministic collection gives a version of Bernstein inequality where all terms are empirical but one, related to the tails of the regeneration times. We then study this term in many regimes: it turns out that it is of second-order in many cases of interest. This is important for applications in machine learning: we prove generalization error bounds for classification with non-i.i.d., regenerative data. These bounds can be used to define learning objectives: by minimizing the first-order term only in the bound, we define agnostic classifiers that still satisfy oracle inequalities. We also show that the bound on the average deviation provided by our results is minimax-optimal in the sample size and in the expected regeneration time. Finally, we combine the Bernstein inequality with a regenerative strong approximation to obtain a Gaussian approximation using an observable block variance estimator.
item.dc:creator: Imon Banerjee, Pierre Alquier

item.title: The maximum distance covariance of bounded random vectors
item.description: arXiv:2306.17067v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A sharp upper bound is obtained for the distance covariance of bounded random vectors in terms of the diameters of their supports alone. The bound is attained for all pairs of support diameter constraints and hence provides the maximum distance covariance subject to constraints of this kind. A normalized measure of dependence is derived by dividing distance covariance by the sharp bound when it is positive. Several properties of the resulting quotient are proved, including domination by distance correlation, invariance under similarities, and subadditivity under sums of independent pairs. The quotient is shown to be nonincreasing under the addition of independent noise, a property not shared by distance correlation. The usual sample distance covariance inherits the sharp bound from the population quantity and the associated normalized statistic is strongly consistent.
item.dc:creator: John \c{C}amk{\i}ran

item.title: Ergodicity for stochastic neural field equations
item.description: arXiv:2505.14012v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the well-posedness and long-time behavior of a general continuum neural field model with Gaussian noise on possibly unbounded domains. In particular, we give conditions for the existence of invariant probability measures by restricting the solution flow to an invariant subspace with a nonlocal metric. Under the assumption of a sufficiently large decay parameter relative to the noise intensity, the norm of the connectivity kernel operator, and the Lipschitz regularity of the activation function, we establish exponential ergodicity and exponential mixing of the associated Markovian Feller semigroup and the uniqueness of the invariant measure.
item.dc:creator: Anna-Mariya Otsetova, Jonas M. T\"olle

item.title: On a class of multiplicative Lindley-type recursions with Markov-modulated dependencies
item.description: arXiv:2508.20495v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study a class of Markov-modulated multiplicative Lindley-type recursions of the form $W_{n+1}=[V_nW_n+Y_n(V_n)]^+$, where the additive term may depend on the multiplicative coefficient and on a common finite-state background Markov chain. The main feature of the model is that the multiplicative coefficient is allowed to take negative values, which destroys the usual monotonicity structure of Lindley-type recursions. We consider two cases. In the first one, $V_n$ may take the values $1$, a constant $a\in(0,1)$, or a negative value, according to specific probabilities, while $Y_n(V_n)=S_n-A_{n+1}$ and the relevant Laplace--Stieltjes transforms are assumed to be rational. In the second one, $V_n\in\{1,-1\}$, and the additive term has a more general form depending on $V_n$. For both models, we derive vector-valued functional equations for the stationary transform. For the first model, we obtain a recursive transform representation, while for the second model we derive a finite-dimensional characterization based on root-cancellation conditions. We also provide a recursive procedure for computing stationary moments and discuss the light-tailed asymptotic behaviour. An extension based on the Farlie--Gumbel--Morgenstern copula is also presented. Numerical experiments show how the transform representation can be used to compute stationary moments, tail probabilities and quantiles, and validate the results against Monte Carlo simulation.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis Dimitriou

item.title: Sharpness of the phase transition for constrained-degree percolation
item.description: arXiv:2509.16162v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider constrained-degree percolation on the hypercubic lattice. Initially, all edges are closed, and each edge independently attempts to open at a uniformly distributed random time; the attempt succeeds if, at that instant, both end-vertices have degrees strictly less than a prescribed parameter. The absence of the FKG inequality and the finite energy property, as well as the infinite range of dependence, make the rigorous analysis of the model particularly challenging. In this work, we show that the one-arm probability exhibits exponential decay in its entire subcritical phase. The proof relies on the Duminil-Copin--Raoufi--Tassion randomized algorithm method and resolves a problem of dos Santos and the second author. At the heart of the argument lies an intricate combinatorial transformation of pivotality in the spirit of Aizenman--Grimmett essential enhancements, but with unbounded range. This technique may be of use in other dynamical settings.
item.dc:creator: Ivailo Hartarsky, Roger W. C. Silva

item.title: Optimal Stopping for the Uniform Distribution
item.description: arXiv:2601.04371v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many discrete-time optimal stopping problems are known to have more tractable limit forms based on a planar Poisson process. Using this tool we find a solution to the optimal stopping problem for i.i.d. sequence of $n$ discrete uniform random variables, in the asymptotic regime where $n$ and the range of distribution are of the same order. The optimal stopping rule in the Poisson problem is identified, by means of a time change, with known asymptotic solution to Lindley's problem of minimising the expected rank.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Gnedin

item.title: An elementary approach to delta and gamma hedging, and the Black--Scholes PDE
item.description: arXiv:2601.08730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show how the robustness of gamma hedging can be understood just using the concepts of $p^{th}$ variation along a partition sequence and Taylor's theorem. There is no need to define an integral or proving a version of It\^o's lemma. The same approach allows classical results on delta-hedging to be proved without defining an integral and without the need to define the concept of self-financing in continuous time. We show that the approach can also be applied to barrier options and Asian options. Finally, we extend the framework to path-dependent derivatives. We introduce a Gubinelli-type control along a sequence of partitions, and use it to define a pathwise notion of arbitrage. Finally, we show that in any arbitrage-free pricing model the greeks must satisfy a linear relation. If one additionally assumes time and scaling symmetries, this yields the Black--Scholes PDE.
item.dc:creator: John Armstrong, Purba Das

item.title: Absolute continuity of the law of the solution to the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation driven by fractional noise
item.description: arXiv:2601.10490v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The stochastic partial differential equation analyzed in this work is the Cahn-Hilliard equation perturbed by an additive fractional white noise (fractional in time and white in space). We work in spatial dimensions $d \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ with $d < 4H$, where $H \in (\frac{1}{2}, 1)$ is the Hurst parameter of the noise, and apply Malliavin calculus to investigate the existence of a density for the solution $u$. In particular, we show that $u$ admits a jointly continuous modification and construct a localizing sequence through which we prove that its Malliavin derivative exists locally, and that its law is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$, thereby establishing that a density exists. We obtain the result for the whole range of dimensions and Hurst parameters in which the mild solution is known to exist. The analysis rests on three new estimates. The first bounds the expectation of the $p$-th power ($p \geq 2$) of the $L^{\infty}(D)$-norm of the stochastic integral appearing in the mild formulation. The other two concern the integral involving the operator associated with the kernel that appears in the integral representation of the fractional noise: an upper estimate and, more importantly, a lower estimate on short time intervals, which yields the nondegeneracy of the Malliavin derivative.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Dimitriou, Dimitris Farazakis, Georgia Karali

item.title: Gaussian Processes with Sample Paths in Reproducing Kernel Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2605.28106v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the connection between Gaussian processes and Gaussian random elements in reproducing kernel Banach spaces. We show that the covariance operator of a weak second-order Radon probability measure on such a space is uniquely determined by a symmetric positive-definite function. In the Gaussian case, we characterize those functions that arise from covariance operators in terms of $\gamma$-radonifying operators. Building on these results, we extend Driscoll's theorem to the reproducing kernel Banach space setting.
item.dc:creator: Toni Karvonen, Rasmus Kleist H{\o}rlyck S{\o}rensen

item.title: Exponential Contraction for Underdamped Langevin Diffusions with Superlinear Forces
item.description: arXiv:2608.10876v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish exponential contraction for underdamped Langevin diffusions with nonconvex confining potentials and possibly superlinear forces. The force satisfies a polynomial local Lipschitz bound with exponent $\ell\geq0$, and the potential has a lower bound of order $m\geq2$, with $3\ell<2m$. Under radial confinement and a potential--dissipation inequality, we construct an explicit weighted Kantorovich transportation cost in which the Markov semigroup contracts probability laws exponentially. The estimate holds for all nonnegative times, with prefactor one and an explicit positive rate, without a smallness condition on the local Lipschitz coefficient. The proof combines localized reflection--synchronous coupling with an exponential Lyapunov weight. A radius-dependent shift of the position--velocity difference balances the local force contribution to the distance drift, while distinct localization scales in position and velocity exploit the growth of the potential. Together, these choices yield a dissipative estimate for the weighted cost with a vanishing regularization error. The regularized couplings preserve the Langevin marginals, so passage to weak limits yields contraction for all initial laws with finite transportation cost. Consequently, the dynamics converge exponentially to the Gibbs measure within the corresponding finite-cost class. The assumptions include quartic double-well potentials of arbitrary amplitude. Numerical experiments for asymmetric quartic wells examine transportation between two initial laws and quantify the conservatism of the explicit rate.
item.dc:creator: Shan Huang, Xiaoyue Li

item.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
item.description: arXiv:2610.15006v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a magma-operad (non-associative partial combination, restricted to the image of disintegration) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding on admissible inputs. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---it defines a renormalization operator $R_{\mathcal{I}}=\text{Combine}\circ\text{Disintegrate}$. The information loss of this operator is exactly the probability curvature $\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{I}}(\mu)$---the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This curvature measures the obstruction to lossless decomposition and reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by CDF-based scalar block summaries.
item.dc:creator: Xuexing Lu

item.title: Scaling Limits of Density Fluctuation Fields of the Symmetric Partial Exclusion Processes Approaching the Zero Range Process
item.description: arXiv:2610.20050v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study equilibrium fluctuations for the symmetric partial exclusion process (SPEP) on the one-dimensional integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, an interacting particle system in which each site is occupied by at most $\alpha$ particles. We assume that the jump rate is decomposable and that the instantaneous current admits a gradient form. Our aim is to study the scaling limit of the density fluctuation field of the SPEP starting from an invariant measure and to derive the corresponding stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE). A distinctive feature of our setting is that the maximum number of particles per site depends on the scaling parameter $n$ as $\alpha=\alpha_n \propto n^a$ for some $a>0$, so that the model interpolates between the partial exclusion process ($\alpha <\infty$) and the symmetric zero range process (SZRP, $\alpha = \infty$). Under the diffusive rescaling in which the lattice spacing is $1/n$ and time is accelerated by a factor $n^2$, we prove that the density fluctuation field converges to the solution of the stochastic heat equation. The limiting SPDE coincides with the one obtained for the SZRP. A key ingredient in the proof is the convergence, under a suitable rescaling, of the partition function of the reversible measure of the SPEP to that of the SZRP. This convergence implies that expectations of a wide class of local functions under the reversible measure of the SPEP converge to the corresponding expectations under the reversible measure of the SZRP, and provides a rigorous sense in which the SPEP approximates the SZRP as $n\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Kanta Nozawa

item.title: On Stopping Sets and Continuous-Time Decision Trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.22011v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study stopping sets and continuous-time decision trees (CTDTs) for Poisson point processes. We prove that every $\mu$-continuous CTDT has an explicit exploration representation: between successive discoveries, the explored set grows according to a deterministic rule depending on the points already observed. If $\mu$ is diffuse, we prove that the points are revealed one by one almost surely; this need not be imposed as a separate assumption. We also allow atoms of $\mu$, in which case all points at one location are revealed together. For diffuse $\mu$, we also prove that a locally bounded stopping set that reveals at most one Poisson point is attainable by a $\mu$-continuous exploration. More generally, an increasing sequence of locally bounded stopping sets, each revealing at most one additional point, can be attained by a single exploration viewed at successive stopping times. Finally, we prove the spatial Markov property of the Poisson point process without assuming that the stopping set contains finitely many points or admits a finite approximation. The proof is based on a general criterion for characterizing conditionally Poisson point processes using moment measures, and uses the multivariate Mecke formula on the complement of the stopping set.
item.dc:creator: Ali Khezeli

item.title: Convergence of the critical probabilities for stopping near the top of a random walk

item.dc:creator: Jos\'e \'Angel Islas

item.title: Large Deviations in Stochastic Dynamics: A Hamiltonian Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2610.27179v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: These lecture notes present an introduction to large deviations in stochastic dynamical systems, adapted from a lecture series given at the Les Houches school ``Large Deviations: Theory and Applications'' in July 2024. The exposition develops the theory through a unified methodology: WKB analysis of backward Kolmogorov equations, which reveals the Hamiltonian structure underlying all large deviation principles considered here. We treat three asymptotic regimes systematically. First, the small-noise limit for stochastic differential equations and the large-volume limit for Markov jump processes, where the Large Deviation Principle emerges from the Law of Large Numbers through progressively finer characterizations of fluctuations. Second, the long-time limit combined with small noise, yielding the quasipotential formalism for metastability and transition rates in both equilibrium and nonequlibrium systems. Third, the long-time limit at finite noise, connecting to spectral methods via tilted generators and enabling reduction of multiscale systems. We survey computational approaches including minimum action methods, their geometric variants for quasipotential calculations, and neural network techniques. The Schl\"{o}gl model of chemical bistability serves as a running example, illustrating both scalar and spatially extended settings. Appendices provide self-contained background on stochastic calculus and Markov jump processes.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Cirigliano, William D. Pi\~{n}eros, Anna Poggialini, Grant M. Rotskoff, Eric Vanden-Eijnden

item.title: Normal approximation for subgraph counts in random intersection graphs: the case of edges
item.description: arXiv:2503.23110v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the subgraph count in the random intersection graph model $\mathcal G(n,m,p)$. Due to substantial edge dependencies, studying even such fundamental statistics is significantly more challenging than in the classical binomial model $\mathcal G(n,p)$. This article establish new normal approximation bounds in both the Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances for general non-degenerate $U$-statistics. We then illustrate how these results can be potentially applied to the standardized number of subgraphs in the random intersection graph model. Finally, as a basic example, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the asymptotic normality of the number of edges in $\mathcal G(n,m,p)$.
item.dc:creator: Katarzyna Rybarczyk, Grzegorz Serafin

item.title: Deterministic algorithms for inhomogeneous Bernoulli trials: Shapley value of network devices
item.description: arXiv:2510.07572v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Suppose that $n$ computer devices are to be connected to a network via inhomogeneous Bernoulli trials. The Shapley value of a device quantifies how much the network's value increases due to the participation of that device. Characteristic functions of such games are naturally taken as the belief function (containment function) and Choquet capacity (hitting probability) of a random set (random network of devices). Traditionally, the Shapley value is either calculated as the expected marginal contribution over all possible coalitions (subnetworks), which results in exponential computational complexity, or approximated by the Monte Carlo sampling technique, where the performance is highly dependent on the stochastic sampling process. The purpose of this study is to design deterministic algorithms for games formulated via inhomogeneous Bernoulli trials that approximate the Shapley value in linear or quadratic time, with rigorous error analysis (Sections 3 and 4). Additionally, we provide a review of relevant literature on existing calculation methods in Remark 3.1 and Appendix I. A further goal is to supplement Shapley's original proof by deriving the Shapley value formula using a rigorous approach based on definite integrals and combinatorial analysis. This method explicitly highlights the roles of the Binomial Theorem and the Beta function in the proof, addressing a gap in Shapley's work (Appendix II).
item.dc:creator: Jesse D Wei, Guo Wei

item.title: Hyperbolic $O (N)$ linear sigma model and its mean-field limit
item.description: arXiv:2511.21950v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study large $N$ limits of the hyperbolic $O(N)$ linear sigma model ($\text{HLSM}_N$) on the two-dimensional torus $\mathbb T^2$, namely, a system of $N$ interacting stochastic damped nonlinear wave equations (SdNLW) with coupled cubic nonlinearities. After establishing (pathwise) global well-posedness of $\text{HLSM}_N$ and the limiting equation, called the mean-field SdNLW, we first establish global-in-time convergence of $\text{HLSM}_N$ to the mean-field SdNLW with general initial data (under a suitable assumption). In particular, for the local-in-time convergence, we obtain a convergence rate of order $N^{- \frac 12}$ under an additional integrability assumption on initial data. We then show that the invariant Gibbs dynamics for $\text{HLSM}_N$ converges to that for the mean-field SdNLW with a convergence rate of order $N^{- \frac 12}$ on any large time intervals.
item.dc:creator: Ruoyuan Liu, Shao Liu, Tadahiro Oh

item.title: Level 2.5 large deviations and uncertainty relations for non-Markov self-interacting dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2601.07943v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We address the general problem of formulating the dynamical large deviations of non-Markovian systems in a closed form. Specifically, we consider a broad class of ``self-interacting'' jump processes whose dynamics depends on the past through a functional of a state-dependent empirical observable. Exploiting a natural separation of timescales, \newnewtext{and under the corresponding mixing conditions,} we obtain the exact (so-called ``level 2.5'') large deviation joint statistics of the empirical measure over configurations and of the empirical flux of transitions. As an application of this general framework, we derive explicit general bounds on the fluctuations of trajectory observables, generalising to the non-Markovian case both thermodynamic and kinetic uncertainty relations. We illustrate our theory with simple examples, and discuss potential applications of these results.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Coghi, Amarjit Budhiraja, Juan P. Garrahan

item.title: Multivariate and quantitative Erd\H{o}s-Kac laws for Beatty sequences
item.description: arXiv:2602.04875v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The classical Erd\H{o}s-Kac theorem states that for $n$ chosen uniformly at random from $1, \dots, N$, the random variable $(\omega(n) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges in distribution to the standard Gaussian as $N$ tends to infinity. Banks and Shparlinski showed that this Gaussian convergence holds for any Beatty sequence $\lfloor\alpha n + \beta\rfloor$ in place of $n$. Continuing in this spirit, Crn\v{c}evi\'c, Hern\'andez, Rizk, Sereesuchart and Tao considered the joint distribution of $\omega(n)$ and $\omega(\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor)$, which they showed to be asymptotically independent for irrational values of $\alpha$. Generalising both results, we show that for any positive integer $k$, real numbers $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k > 0$ and $\beta_1, \dots, \beta_k$, where $\alpha_i/\alpha_j$ is irrational for $i\neq j$, the joint distribution of $(\omega(\lfloor\alpha_in + \beta_i\rfloor) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges to the $k$-dimensional standard Gaussian. We next discuss quantitative bounds on the rate of convergence which do not depend on the values taken by the relevant parameters. Banks and Shparlinski remarked that such quantitative bounds may be given for a single Beatty sequence $\lfloor\alpha n + \beta\rfloor$ under Diophantine type assumptions on $\alpha$. We show that such assumptions are in fact unnecessary. Specifically, for any real numbers $\alpha > 0, \beta$, we show that the Kolmogorov distance between the random variable $(\omega(\lfloor\alpha n + \beta\rfloor) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ and the standard Gaussian is bounded above by $O(\log\log\log N/\sqrt{\log\log N})$ as $N$ tends to infinity. On the other hand, we show that universal quantitative bounds of this kind do not exist for higher-degree generalised polynomials or for the joint convergence for multiple Beatty sequences.

item.title: Depth dependence of entanglement and circuit complexity in random linear optical networks
item.description: arXiv:2604.14277v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the growth of entanglement and circuit complexity in random passive linear optical networks as a function of the circuit depth. For entanglement dynamics, we start with an initial Gaussian state with all $n$ modes equally squeezed. For random brickwork circuits, we show that entanglement, as measured by the R\'enyi-2 entropy, grows diffusively as a function of the depth, in contrast to the linear growth for random qubit brickwork circuits. In the other direction, for arbitrary circuit geometries we prove bounds on depths which ensure the average-case subsystem entanglement reaches within a constant factor of the maximum value in all subsystems, and bounds which ensure closeness of the random linear optical unitary to a Haar random unitary in $L^2$ Wasserstein distance. We also consider robust circuit complexity for random one-dimensional brickwall circuits, as measured by the minimum number of gates required in any circuit that approximately implements the linear optical unitary. Viewing this as a function of the number of modes and the circuit depth, we show the robust circuit complexity for random one-dimensional brickwall circuits scales at most diffusively in the depth with high probability, again in contrast to the linear scaling for certain random qubit circuits. The corresponding Gaussian unitary $\tilde{\mathcal U}$ for the approximate implementation retains high output fidelity $|\langle\psi|\mathcal U^\dagger \tilde{\mathcal U}|\psi\rangle|^2$ for pure states $|\psi\rangle$ with constrained expected photon-number.

item.title: Kinetic theory for Transformers and the lost-in-the-middle phenomenon
item.description: arXiv:2605.09213v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study causal self-attention dynamics -- a toy model for decoder Transformers -- which we interpret as a non-exchangeable interacting particle system. Adapting cumulant expansions to the triangular causal dependency structure of the model, and appealing to non-hierarchical methods to estimate correlations using Glauber calculus, we prove a quantitative mean-field limit result and a next-order characterization of correlations. For iid uniformly distributed tokens, the limiting correlation equation can be solved in closed form and we obtain a rigorous explanation of the empirically observed \emph{lost-in-the-middle} phenomenon: the token retrieval profile, as a function of the source position in the prompt, is $\mathsf{U}$-shaped, with primacy, recency, and a unique interior minimum under an explicit smallness condition.

item.title: Non-symmetric vector dyson equations
item.description: arXiv:2607.16333v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the vector Dyson equation $$-\frac{1}{m(z)}=z\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{a}+Sm(z),$$ with parameter $z$ in the complex upper half-plane $\mathbb{C}_+$, where $\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb R^d$ and $S$ is a nonnegative matrix, not necessarily symmetric. This equation has a unique vector solution $m(z)\in\mathbb{C}_+^d$, for which we establish a complete measure decomposition and prove regularity. We then develop a graph-theoretic approach to the singularity and stability problem for non-symmetric matrices $S$. The graph structure of $S$ identifies the possible degeneracies of the stability operator as $z$ approaches the real axis. In particular, for non-backtracking matrices, we prove square-root growth at regular edges, cubic-root growth at regular cusps, and complete stability estimates. We also obtain the corresponding estimates for symmetric matrices in the periodic setting.

item.title: Poincar\'e Beta Balls: Radial Laws, Hyperbolic Shell Metric Transforms, and Critical-Limit Regimes
item.description: arXiv:2607.26979v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: On a high-dimensional Poincar\'e ball, a Euclidean beta-type radial measure concentrates near a sphere, but hyperbolic distance amplifies the surviving radial spread, so the usual shell reduction loses part of the limiting metric. In each regime of the balance between this radial width and amplified angular separation, we determine the weak pyramid limit of the spaces rescaled at the order at which the transition between concentration and dissipation occurs. The four critical-limit regimes are the shifted-exponential railway pyramid, the diameter-at-most-one regime, the nonlinear Gaussian-transform regime, and the Gaussian regime. Each finite-branch railway mm-space generating the first pyramid has branches from a common center, a shifted exponential distribution along them, and paths between different branches through the center. We also give a sharp criterion for convergence to the diameter-at-most-one pyramid. The resulting classification identifies the precise critical scales and clarifies when angular and radial fluctuations contribute simultaneously to the limiting geometry.

item.title: Optimal concentration and gradient sensing by perfect monitors
item.description: arXiv:2608.08816v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cells often estimate chemical concentrations from only a few diffusing molecules, whose stochastic motion limits sensing precision. We consider a perfect monitoring instrument that records the instantaneous molecular density throughout a finite region without perturbing the concentration field or distinguishing molecular identities. The standard Berg-Purcell estimator weights all positions uniformly. Here we derive the optimal spatial weighting within a large class of unbiased estimators for both concentration and gradient sensing. Variance minimization maps to an electrostatic problem. Surprisingly, although the instrument monitors the entire volume, the optimal estimator assigns all weight to its boundary, reducing the uncertainty in both concentration and gradient sensing. We extend the results to arbitrary geometries and spatial dimensions.

item.title: Quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation for unregularized Vlasov-Riesz-Fokker-Planck systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.23709v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation for the unregularized repulsive Vlasov--Riesz--Fokker--Planck system on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$. For product initial data and potentials with singularity $|x|^{-s}$, $0<s<d/2$, we obtain an algebraic convergence rate for the $k$-particle marginals on a time interval independent of the particle number. The constants grow at most exponentially in $k$. The three-dimensional Coulomb case gives every rate $N^{-b}$ with $0<b<1/3$. The assumptions on its limiting solution hold for weighted Sobolev data with a Gaussian velocity moment and, on $\mathbb{R}^3$, a polynomial spatial moment. The proof combines conditioning of the initial product law, auxiliary particle equations, and weighted BBGKY estimates. An $L^1$ estimate and pointwise exponential energy bounds control the remainder flux in weighted $L^q$. For correlated initial data satisfying pointwise energy and marginal error bounds, the comparison extends to $0<s<d-1$.

item.title: Spectral theory for dynamical large deviations in non-Markov self-interacting processes
item.description: arXiv:2609.40329v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a spectral theory for dynamical large deviations in non-Markov jump processes and non-Markov chains, whose dynamics depends on the past through state- and jump-dependent empirical observables. We demonstrate that a multiscale Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin-Jeffreys (WKBJ) Ansatz separates fast configurational relaxation from slow memory evolution, reducing the Feynman--Kac equation for occupation and flux statistics to an eigenvalue problem for a new tilted operator coupled to Hamilton--Jacobi characteristics. This provides a computationally efficient framework for quantifying fluctuations in a broad class of non-Markovian systems. We illustrate our general results with a bistable self-induced East model.

item.title: GROMM: Generative Risk-neutral Option Market Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.16732v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a statically and dynamically arbitrage-free European option market model with smooth interpolation between option prices, based on the SANOS framework, and prove that its dynamics admit a unique strong solution. In spirit, it is a stochastic model for local volatility when the latter is used as a representation of a European option price surface, not as a pricing model. We illustrate the strength of our approach on S&P Index Option data from January 2022 to August 2025. We show that the model's initial state fits within bid/ask for more than 95% of relevant market option prices. We then train the model dynamics under $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ and show that the model is indeed free of arbitrage while fitting the dynamics of the market well. We also propose a range of BHW-tests to test for absence of arbitrage.
